US-119-HR10061.title: Wildfire Response and Readiness Act

actions.text: Referred to the Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity.

Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources, and in addition to the Committees on Agriculture, Transportation and Infrastructure, Small Business, Science, Space, and Technology, Energy and Commerce, Education and Workforce, Veterans' Affairs, and Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

US-119-HR10061.description: To address wildfire readiness and recovery, safe communities, and wildland firefighter safety.
US-119-HR10061.aiSummary: The bill would expand federal work on wildfire prevention, recovery, and response. It would support prescribed fire, forest restoration, community wildfire defense grants, smoke monitoring, wildfire research, and new tools for detection and mapping. It would also set new steps for wildland firefighter pay, leave, health, retirement, and workforce support.

US-119-HR10083.title: Water Technology and Resilience Reauthorization Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

US-119-HR10083.description: To reauthorize appropriations for the advanced drinking water technology grant program under the Safe Drinking Water Act, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10083.aiSummary: The bill would renew funding authority for a grant program for advanced drinking water technology under the Safe Drinking Water Act. It would change the covered years from 2022 through 2026 to 2027 through 2031, affecting that grant program and the agencies that run it.

US-119-HR9490.title: Bank Failure Accountability Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
Sponsor introductory remarks on measure. (CR H4251)

US-119-HR9490.description: To defer part of the compensation of senior employees of large financial institutions (and their subsidiaries), to use such deferred amounts to pay any civil or criminal fines that may be levied on the institution (or subsidiary), and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9490.aiSummary: The bill would require large financial institutions and their subsidiaries to hold back part of pay for certain senior employees. The held-back money would be used first to pay civil or criminal fines, and for some banks or credit unions that fail, to help make depositors whole. It would apply to financial firms with more than $1 billion in assets, with different rules based on firm size and employee pay.
